incidente.resumo: A failure of a component on a fiber path from a central US gateway campus in Google's production backbone reduced available bandwidth to multiple edge locations, causing 20 minutes of intermittent packet loss for traffic between multiple Google Cloud regions. Automated repair mechanisms rerouted the traffic through alternate links without manual intervention; an incomplete network augmentation forced some traffic onto the third-best path and extended the migration.

descricao.texto: Google's automated repair mechanisms detected the decrease in available network bandwidth on 20 May 2022 at 13:47 US/Pacific.
trechos: Google’s automated repair mechanisms detected the decrease in available network bandwidth on Friday, 20 May 2022 at 13:47 US/Pacific and automatically routed the traffic through alternate links.

descricao.texto: A failure of a component on a fiber path from one of the central US gateway campuses in Google's production backbone decreased available network bandwidth between the gateway and multiple edge locations, causing packet loss while the backbone automatically moved traffic onto remaining paths.
trechos: A failure of a component on a fiber path from one of the central US gateway campuses in Google’s production backbone led to a decrease in available network bandwidth between the gateway and multiple edge locations, causing packet loss while the backbone automatically moved traffic onto remaining paths.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The network topology in this region was being augmented and the second-best path had not completed its augmentation, so some traffic needed to reroute onto the third-best path, which led to an extended traffic migration period.
trechos: The network topology in this region is being augmented, and the second-best path has not completed its augmentation.
This meant some traffic needed to reroute onto the third-best path, which led to an extended traffic migration period.

passos.texto: Google's automated repair mechanisms automatically routed the traffic through alternate links, without manual intervention; the rerouting completed at 14:06 US/Pacific, mitigating the issue.
trechos: Google’s automated repair mechanisms detected the decrease in available network bandwidth on Friday, 20 May 2022 at 13:47 US/Pacific and automatically routed the traffic through alternate links.
The traffic rerouting completed on Friday, 20 May 2022 at 14:06 US/Pacific, mitigating the issue.
While our automated mechanisms worked as intended and recovered the traffic without manual intervention, we understand that the scope of impact caused by this event affected our customers.

acoes.texto: Complete the network augmentation in this region by 11 July 2022, returning to the intended topology where any single fiber path failure can be rerouted quickly onto the second-best path.
trechos: In this network region, we intend to complete the augmentation by 11 July 2022, which will return the network to the intended topology where any single fiber path failure can be rerouted quickly onto the second-best path.

acoes.texto: Build automatic analysis to ensure that the network topology during augmentation always supports fast convergence.
trechos: We will also build automatic analysis to ensure that the network topology during augmentation always supports fast convergence.

acoes.texto: Ongoing work to optimize the global network to minimize the time spent automatically reconfiguring around failures (convergence time).
trechos: We have been working on optimizing our global network to minimize the time spent automatically reconfiguring around failures like this (known as "convergence time").
While we have made progress, efforts to improve are ongoing.
On Friday, 20 May 2022 at 13:47 US/Pacific, Google Cloud Networking experienced intermittent packet loss for traffic between multiple cloud regions for a duration of 20 minutes.

observacoes: The document combines status updates, a preliminary mini incident report (which, from preliminary analysis, attributed the cause to a hardware issue on an optical amplification component in the backbone) and a final incident report. dominio is infra_fisica_datacenter as the origin is a physical network component failure in the backbone, although the fiber path is between campuses rather than strictly inside a data center.
